metadata.name: Protocol and Codec Assignment Rules
metadata.description: Full signaling/media protocol and codec catalog, assignment strategies, popularity distributions, compatibility rules, and compatibility matrix. Authoritative over Step 2's simplified per-scenario codec_distribution blocks.

signaling_protocols.name: Session Initiation Protocol
signaling_protocols.notes: Dominant/primary protocol across all scenario profiles.

signaling_protocols.name: H.323
signaling_protocols.notes: Legacy ITU-T signaling suite; retained for legacy-infrastructure realism.

media_protocols.name: Secure RTP
media_protocols.notes: Requires a resolved key-exchange mechanism whenever assigned.

codecs.name: G.722
codecs.typical_use: HD voice, conference rooms, clinical consultation

codecs.name: SPEEX
codecs.typical_use: Open-source legacy codec, superseded by Opus

codecs.name: Comfort Noise
codecs.typical_use: Synthetic background noise during silence suppression (DTX/VAD)

codec_assignment_strategies.name: Uniform Distribution
codec_assignment_strategies.description: Equal selection probability across all codecs in the configured candidate list.
codec_assignment_strategies.when_used: Test/POC datasets, synthetic-noise baselines, or when no realistic device/infrastructure mix is known or desired.

codec_assignment_strategies.name: Weighted Distribution
codec_assignment_strategies.description: Fixed global weights reflecting general real-world codec popularity, applied regardless of environment.
codec_assignment_strategies.when_used: Default fallback when an environment has no explicit override; generic non-scenario-specific datasets.

codec_assignment_strategies.name: Environment-Specific Distribution
codec_assignment_strategies.description: Per-scenario weight tables reflecting that environment's device mix, network conditions, and infrastructure age.
codec_assignment_strategies.when_used: Default and recommended strategy for all six named scenario profiles (Step 2).

comfort_noise_usage_probability.description: Independent probability (not part of the codec weight sum) that a given call, given DTX/silence-suppression is supported, attaches Comfort Noise alongside its primary codec.

compatibility_rules.rule: Any call with media_protocol=SRTP must resolve an encryption method (AES) and a key-exchange mechanism (SDES-SRTP or DTLS-SRTP).
Any assigned codec must belong to the codecs list in this document; assignment outside this list is invalid.
Comfort Noise may only be attached alongside a primary speech codec when DTX/silence-suppression is modeled; it cannot be the sole codec for a call.

If signaling_protocol=H.323, media_protocol is forced to RTP regardless of the environment's SRTP weight, since H.323's native encryption path (H.235) is distinct from SRTP and is out of scope for the default profiles.
AMR-NB and AMR-WB should only be assigned when the call's network context is mobile/cellular-gateway-originated, not internal desk-phone segments.
Bandwidth-constrained (remote/VPN/WAN) network segments should upweight low-bitrate codecs (G.729, AMR-NB, iLBC, low-bitrate-mode Opus) and downweight high-bitrate codecs (G.711, G.722).
GSM, G.723.1, SILK, iSAC, and SPEEX receive low baseline weight by default and should only be upweighted for datasets explicitly modeling legacy infrastructure.
Codec sample rate must match its stated type (narrowband=8kHz, wideband=16kHz); Opus alone spans 8-48kHz and is resolved per-call based on negotiated mode.

compatibility_matrix.notes: Proprietary lineage; non-standard on classic SIP trunks
Not natively defined in classic H.323 codec tables
